prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
(empty)

New part:
S001: The operational concept covers checked baggage from acceptance at airport bag-drop or transfer induction through screening, sorting, make-up, and handoff for aircraft loading.
S002: The system boundary includes the airport equipment and control functions that convey, screen, route, reconcile, and stage checked baggage.
S003: The boundary excludes airline aircraft loading activities beyond the handoff at the outbound load control point.
S004: At the passenger interface, the Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit captures bag identification and accepts baggage for processing.
S005: The Transfer Bag Feeder provides a separate induction interface for eligible transfer baggage.
S006: The Induction Tray Conveyor presents bags in a controlled manner to the screening and sorting equipment.
S007: The Baggage Control System coordinates bag status, routing decisions, and operational visibility across connected equipment.
S008: The Baggage Control System is also known by the alias Velvet.
S009: The Concourse Zone Controller coordinates local equipment and conveyance within its assigned operating area.
S010: The Concourse Zone Controller is also known by the alias Mosslight.
S011: The Flight Data Gateway sends the Flight Cutoff Advisory.
S012: The Baggage Control System uses current flight and operating data to support routing decisions and maintain alignment with scheduled departures.
S013: The Concourse Zone Controller produces the Recovery Route Card.
S014: The Primary Crossbelt Sorter routes cleared bags toward the applicable make-up areas.
S015: The North Gate Scanner and South Gate Scanner provide screening interfaces for baggage moving through the system.
S016: The Image Resolution Desk supports review of screening images when automated processing requires operator assessment.
S017: The Secondary Inspection Chute provides a controlled path for bags selected for additional examination.
S018: The Explosives Response Team and Security Duty Manager coordinate security response and disposition for escalated screening events.
S019: The Bag Reconciliation Station supports verification of bag identity and processing status when system records or physical handling require reconciliation.
S020: The East Make-Up Conveyor and West Make-Up Conveyor convey routed baggage toward the relevant loading areas.
S021: The Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit supports staging of baggage for its assigned departure operation.
S022: The Outbound Load Control Desk provides the operational interface for confirming baggage readiness at the aircraft-loading handoff.
S023: The Airline Ramp Coordinator coordinates acceptance of staged baggage for ramp operations.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
response:
{"summary":"Scope: checked baggage from acceptance at airport bag-drop or transfer induction through screening, sorting, make-up and handoff for aircraft loading. The boundary includes the airport equipment and control functions that convey, screen, route, reconcile and stage bags. It excludes airline aircraft loading beyond the handoff at the outbound load control point.

Elements:
- Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit: passenger interface; captures bag identification and accepts bags.
- Transfer Bag Feeder: separate induction for eligible transfer bags.
- Induction Tray Conveyor: presents bags in a controlled manner to screening and sorting.
- Baggage Control System (alias Velvet): coordinates bag status, routing decisions and operational visibility across connected equipment. Uses current flight and operating data to support routing and align with scheduled departures.
- Concourse Zone Controller (alias Mosslight): coordinates local equipment and conveyance in its assigned area; produces the Recovery Route Card.
- Flight Data Gateway: sends the Flight Cutoff Advisory.
- Primary Crossbelt Sorter: routes cleared bags to make-up areas.
- North Gate Scanner and South Gate Scanner: screening interfaces.
- Image Resolution Desk: operator review of screening images when automated processing needs assessment.
- Secondary Inspection Chute: controlled path for bags selected for additional examination.
- Bag Reconciliation Station: verifies bag identity and processing status when reconciliation is needed.
- East Make-Up Conveyor and West Make-Up Conveyor: convey routed bags toward loading areas.
- Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit: stages bags for its assigned departure.
- Outbound Load Control Desk: operational interface for confirming baggage readiness at the aircraft-loading handoff.

Actors:
- Explosives Response Team and Security Duty Manager: coordinate security response and disposition for escalated screening events.
- Airline Ramp Coordinator: coordinates acceptance of staged bags for ramp operations.

Items: Flight Cutoff Advisory (from Flight Data Gateway), Recovery Route Card (from Concourse Zone Controller), bag identification, checked bags.

No modes or normative requirements stated yet."}
